next.title: What to do now
very_high: Do not send money, OTPs or bank details.
End the call or chat. Do not stay on the video call.
Tell a family member right away.
high: Do not pay anything until you have verified this.
Check using the official website or phone number, not the one in the message.
Call 1930 if you are unsure or have already paid.
medium: Do not click links or pay until you have checked.
Verify with the official source: their website, or the number on your bank card.
cannot_verify: Take a clearer, full photo and try again, or paste the text.
Verify with the official helpline before paying.
low: No major warning signs were found, but this is not a guarantee.

dossier.title: Evidence summary
dossier.disclaimer: Prepared by you for your records and to help when you report. This is not an FIR or an official complaint.
dossier.summaryTemplate: On {{date}} I received a {{kind}} that I believe is a scam. Kavach showed this risk level: {{level}}. I prepared this summary myself.
dossier.evidenceHint: A fingerprint (SHA-256) is worked out on your phone from each file. It helps show later that your original was not changed.
dossier.keepOriginals: Keep your original photos, screenshots and chats on your phone. We delete our copy.
dossier.scriptTitle: What to say to the helpline
dossier.script: Hello, I want to report a cyber fraud. On {{date}} I sent {{amount}} to UPI ID {{upi}}. The transaction reference (UTR) is {{utr}}. The scammer's phone number is {{phone}}. Please help me stop this payment.

sentMoney.title: Already sent money?
sentMoney.subtitle: Act fast. Reporting quickly gives the best chance of stopping the transfer, but nothing is guaranteed.

call.title: Call 1930 right now
call.detail: This is the national cyber fraud helpline. Tell them the amount, the time and the UPI ID.

report.title: Report on cybercrime.gov.in
report.detail: File a complaint online and keep the acknowledgement number.

bank.title: Call your bank
bank.detail: Use the number on your card or the bank's official website. Ask them to hold or flag the transaction.

evidence.title: Save the evidence
evidence.detail: Take screenshots of the payment, the bank SMS, the UTR number, the UPI ID, the phone number and the chats.

keep.title: Do not delete anything
keep.detail: Keep chats, call logs and the original files. Do not reset your phone.

nomore.title: Do not send more money
nomore.detail: Scammers often promise to return your money for a fee. Do not pay again.

history.title: History
history.subtitle: We keep only the type, risk level and time. Files and details are deleted after 15 minutes.
history.emptyBody: When you check something, it will appear here.
history.confirmBody: This removes your list of past checks from this device. This cannot be undone.

q1.q: Do police arrest people over a video call?
q1.a: No. Police and courts do not carry out a "digital arrest" over a video call, and they do not ask you to transfer money to avoid arrest. Anyone who does is trying to scam you.

q2.a: No. You can check without an account. An account only keeps your language and history on every device.

q3.a: It is used only to check it and is deleted automatically within 15 minutes. Your history keeps only the type, risk level and time, and you can delete that too.

q4.a: Open "Already sent money?" on the home screen and follow the steps. Call 1930 right away.

q5.a: Kavach gives a risk assessment with reasons, not a verdict. It can be wrong. Always verify with an official source before paying.
